History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old known asthmatic reports 2–3-day history of new wheeze, dry cough and exertional dyspnoea minimally responsive to salbutamol; assessed via video, likely mild asthma exacerbation, stepped-up inhaled steroids advised and urgent in-person review arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough.  
• Onset/progression: Began 2–3 days ago while running; now symptomatic with brisk walking. No baseline symptoms when walking previously.  
• Relievers tried: Salbutamol (blue inhaler) used PRN daily; little benefit.  
• Associated symptoms: Wheeze, dry cough; denies sputum production. No chest pain, fever, or hospital admission.  
• Triggers/relievers: Exercise precipitates; no specific allergen noted; preventer inhaler may have been under-dosed.  
• Last asthma attack: 3–4 years ago; managed with inhalers only, no oral steroids.  
• Peak-flow: Usual ~380 L/min (patient estimate); no recent reading.  
• Asthma review: Last review 2 years ago.  
• Pertinent negatives: No prior oral steroids, no medication allergies, no sputum, no fever.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – generally well-controlled until current episode; no prior hospitalisations.  
• Hay fever (allergic rhinitis).  
• Possible eczema (self-reported skin patches; using emollients/topical steroid).

Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented) – currently PRN, up to every 2 hrs advised.  
• Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler, previously 3 puffs BID; plan to increase to 4 puffs BID.  
• Cetraben cream (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Topical hydrocortisone (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies reported.

Social History:
• Physically active runner.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: not discussed.  
• Lives at home; no social or financial concerns mentioned.

Family History:
• Brother – asthma.  
• Sister – eczema.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (video consult).  
• Chest/other exam: Not performed (tele-consultation).

Investigations:
• None conducted; plan for peak-flow and chest examination at face-to-face review.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Likely mild asthma exacerbation (loss of control possibly triggered by exercise or allergen), currently without red-flag features but requiring stepped-up inhaled steroids and close follow-up.

DDx Integration:
1. Asthma exacerbation – strong history of asthma, acute wheeze/SOB, poor relief with reliever.  
2. Viral URTI triggering asthma – acute onset, cough; no systemic viral symptoms (opposing).  
3. Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction / poor inhaler technique – symptoms began with running, but now occur at lower exertion (opposing).

Issue 1: Asthma exacerbation
• Plan:
  – Increase Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily.  
  – Continue salbutamol PRN; may use up to every 2 hours short-term.  
  – Arrange face-to-face GP review within a few days for chest exam and peak-flow; consider oral steroids +/- antibiotics depending on findings.  
  – Safety-net: Attend A&E immediately if breathlessness worsens or salbutamol needed more frequently than every 2 hrs.

Issue 2: Asthma monitoring / preventive care
• Plan:
  – Schedule formal asthma review (spirometry, inhaler technique check, action plan).  
  – Reinforce regular preventer use and correct inhaler technique.

Issue 3: Atopic conditions (hay fever / possible eczema)
• Plan:
  – Continue Cetraben and topical hydrocortisone as needed.  
  – Consider allergen review if seasonal triggers suspected.

General plan items
• Confirm medication list and allergies at next visit.  
• Provide written asthma action plan and peak-flow diary.

Quality checks:
● No vitals or physical examination documented – expected to be completed at face-to-face review.  
● Social history (smoking/alcohol) not obtained.  
● Medication doses/routes largely unspecified; to be reconciled.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; minor inaudible sections but core information intact.
